aiOverview.content: As of March 2026, roughly 95% of TSA employees are working without pay due to a partial government shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Congress has failed to pass funding for the department due to disputes over immigration, making TSA employees, who are deemed essential, work without pay while awaiting future back pay. Key Reasons for Unpaid Status: Congressional Impasse: A deadlock between lawmakers over funding for the DHS, specifically regarding immigration policies, has resulted in a lapse in funding, according to YouTube video and reports from KSL.com. Essential Personnel Status: TSA agents are considered "essential," meaning they are required to report for duty to ensure national security, despite not receiving regular paychecks, say reports from The Coloradoan and Fortune. Repeated Funding Lapses: This is the third funding lapse for TSA employees in six months, causing significant financial stress, say reports from CNN and CNN. Impact on Workers: Financial Crisis: Many workers are facing immense financial strain, with some struggling to pay for fuel to commute to work, according to Instagram posts and CNN. Workforce Shortages: At least 366 TSA officers have resigned since the shutdown began, and higher-than-normal "call-out" rates (over 9%) are causing longer airport wait times, say reports from CNN and CBS News. Workers will receive back pay once a funding bill is passed, but the timing for this is currently unknown, notes a report from Facebook.
